title: Quick actions & templates for API fallout
body:
Purpose: quick, copy-paste action items and short templates to shave minutes off common API incidents (client timeouts, 429s/rate-limits, degraded streaming chunks, elevated 5xx/error rates). This is intentionally terse — use as a pocket-runbook during PagerDuty rotations.

How to use: pick the section that best matches symptoms, run the immediate actions in order, then move to investigation checklist. If you hit an obvious fix (eg. scale up or toggle fallback) note it in the incident channel and mark Status=stabilized.

-----
Immediate triage summary (0–10 minutes)
- Who: grab primary oncall + owner from the most recent deploy (check deploy metadata).
- Channel: create incident channel #incident-api-<short-id> and invite eng-sre, infra, product-owner.
- PagerDuty: acknowledge and set severity (S1/S2) per impact matrix below.
- Short status post: "Observing increased API errors/timeouts affecting X% of requests, interventions: investigating. Triage checklist running."

Severity impact matrix (quick):
- S1: >20% of production requests failing or all customer-facing routes returning 5xx / hard timeouts for multiple customers -> Full incident.
- S2: 5–20% of requests affected or a single critical customer severely impacted -> Scoped incident.
- S3: <5% or non-critical background jobs -> Monitor + Investigate.

-----
Templates for immediate actions by symptom (copy/paste form)
A) Client timeouts (requests hitting server-level deadline or network idle)
1) Confirm: tail logs for 500/timeout patterns: kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=api-gateway --since=10m | grep -E "context deadline|timeout|504"
2) Check pod resource pressure: kubectl top pods -n inference | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 10
3) Check upstream engine latency (model pool): curl -s http://engine-metrics.internal/latency | jq '.p95'
4) Temporary mitigation: deploy a short-lived route-level timeout increase (config route X: timeout 60s -> 90s) OR enable "fast-fallback" path to smaller model variant. Command: curl -X POST $ADMIN_API/routes/X/config -d '{"timeout_s":90}'
5) If CPU or mem saturated: scale horizontally: kubectl scale deployment api-gateway --replicas=$((current+2))
6) If network congestion suspected: toggle region fallback to nearest healthy region: /admin/fallback/enable?region=us-west-2
7) Post in channel: action taken, metrics links, owner.

B) 429s / Rate-limited responses
1) Confirm client-facing 429s via logs: kubectl -n inference logs -l route=<route> --since=5m | grep "HTTP/1.1\" 429"
2) Check quota/rl configuration: curl -s $ADMIN_API/quotas/route/<route>
3) Short mitigations:
   - Increase per-route token/quota temporarily (admin UI or API).
   - Enable burst override policy: POST $ADMIN_API/policies/override -d '{"route":"<route>","burst":true,"duration_s":600}'
   - Apply client-side backpressure guidance: send immediate advisory to clients in channel with recommended retry-after header use.
4) Long-term note: add missing client-retrofit tickets if clients are retrying aggressively.

C) Degraded streaming (chunks delayed / truncated)
1) Confirm: check streaming worker logs and connection resets: kubectl logs -l component=stream-worker --since=5m | grep -E "reset|closed|chunk"
2) Check connection counts and per-connection memory: curl -s http://streaming-metrics/conn | jq '.active'
3) Short mitigations:
   - Flip to chunked fallback: admin toggle stream_chunked=true for route (keeps progress but reduces memory pressure).
   - Reduce max_concurrent_streams on fronting proxies to keep latency stable.
   - If NVMe-backed cache is hit rate-limited, temporarily increase KV cache size for prefix caching.
4) If streaming workers OOM: rollout to previous revision or scale worker pool by +30% until root cause identified.

D) Elevated error rate (5xx surge)
1) Confirm scope: sample errors by code: curl -s $METRICS_API/errors?since=10m | head -n 50
2) Identify correlated changes: recent deploys (git tag), infra changes, config rollouts in last 30m: curl -s $ADMIN_API/audit?since=30m
3) Short mitigations:
   - Automatic rollback of last deploy if error spike aligns with new revision. Command: /admin/rollout/rollback?service=api-gateway&to=previous
   - Activate circuit breaker: set route-level failure threshold to 50% for 10m and divert to safe-path.
   - Enable model-variant degrade: switch calls to quantized/cheaper variant to reduce failure surface.
4) If third-party dependency causing errors, switch to cached/replicated fallback path (serve last-good response template) and notify partner.

-----
Investigation checklist (10–60 minutes)
- Confirm scope: percentage errors by route, region, customer (get from dashboards).
- Correlate latency/throughput: p50/p95/p99 for downstream model pools and database/kv.
- Recent code/config changes: review last 2 deploys and feature flags.
- Resource saturation: CPU/GPU/Memory/I/O across API and engine nodes.
- SLO hit calculation: compute projected burn for next 24h.
- Are retries/backpressure loops causing amplified traffic? Use sampling to inspect client retry headers.
- Check autoscaler logs and decisions (scale-up throttles, cooldowns).
- Confirm that fallback policies are reachable (no ACL or network blocking).

Quick commands (reference):
- kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide
- kubectl describe pod <pod> -n inference
- kubectl logs -n inference <pod> -c api --tail=200
- curl -s $METRICS_API/summary | jq .
- tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/api-gateway.log | grep -i error

-----
Escalation and comms templates
- Short incident status update: "T+15m: Elevated 5xx across /v1/generate affecting ~12% of requests. Temporary mitigations applied: scaled api-gateway +2 replicas and enabled model-variant fallback for high-latency routes. Investigating deploys and engine latency."
- Executive summary (for +2 hours): one paragraph with impact, customers affected, mitigation, next steps, ETA for fix.
- Customer-facing message (if needed): "We're currently experiencing higher-than-normal error rates affecting some API requests. We're actively mitigating and expect restoration within X hours. We will follow up with a root cause once confirmed."

-----
Post-incident capture (use this template in the incident channel)
- Title: concise incident name
- Start: ISO timestamp
- Impact: S1/S2/S3 + short bullets (routes/customers)
- Actions taken: ordered list with timestamps
- Root cause hypothesis: initial and final (update after RCA)
- Rollback/patch: links to PRs or config changes
- Engineering owner: name + pager duty reference
- Follow-ups: tickets created, owners, due dates
- Retro notes: what went well, what failed, automation opportunities

-----
Tactical notes / gotchas observed in past incidents (short list)
- Aggressive client retries can amplify a small transient into full-blown overload. If you see many quick retries, implement client advisory + server-side short-circuit.
- Increasing timeouts without addressing root cause can mask failure and worsen resource contention. Prefer capacity or fallback first.
- Streaming truncation often correlates with upstream model GC or KV evictions; look for sudden LRU evictions on caches.
- 429s sometimes caused by a single noisy API key — use per-api-key dashboards to identify and throttle.

-----
Open items to convert into engineering tickets
- Add a route-level "safe-mode" toggle to automatically enable fallback when p95 engine latency > 3s for 5m.
- Make per-client retry headers visible in logs and trace spans.
- Add a lightweight health endpoint for streaming workers that includes active connection count and memory pressure.

-----
Appendix: quick checklist to paste into an incident channel
- [ ] Channel created: #incident-<id>
- [ ] Pager acknowledged
- [ ] Primary owner assigned
- [ ] Short status posted
- [ ] Immediate mitigation applied (scale/rollback/fallback)
- [ ] Errors reduced (observe metrics)
- [ ] RCA ticket created

If you used a mitigation that will impact cost (scale/replicas, increased cache), call out in the postmortem and notify finance/ops leads.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc intentionally terse; longer form runbooks for each subsystem live in confluence link above. If you add a new quick-action, add it as a bullet under the relevant symptom and ping the SRE guild for review.
